lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.19 - A Look & write

details: Look and write gives controlled writing practice with past-tense verbs and feeling adjectives, helping students describe amusement-park activities with accurate word choice and spelling.
Look for correct word choices, complete sentences that match the pictures, past-tense verbs and adjectives used accurately, and neat, legible handwriting.

“I liked the amusement park so much… I went to another one! What animals can you see at the petting zoo? Look at the people here… how do they feel? I want to know all about their day. Let’s help them finish the sentences about what they did and how they felt.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.19 - B. Listen & choose

details: Listen and choose develops listening comprehension of past-tense sentences by training students to identify key words and match them to the correct amusement-park pictures.
Look for careful listening and prompt selection of the correct picture with few mistakes.
“Close your eyes and listen. Some children are talking about their day at the amusement park. Can you choose the right picture for them?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - A Match & Write

details: Match and write reinforces recognition and creation of full past-tense sentences about amusement-park activities and feelings, linking each sentence clearly to a supporting picture.
Look for accurate matching, correct copying of all words and punctuation, and sentences that clearly fit each picture.
“These children are looking at their photos from the amusement park. The sentences are ready, but they are mixed up. Can you match each sentence to the right picture and write it neatly?”

Unscramble focuses on word order in the past simple, building accuracy with questions and statements, capital letters, and end punctuation.
Look for correct word order, use of capital letters, question marks and full stops, and clear sentences and questions that make sense.
“Oh no, the words in this notebook are all in the wrong order! Can you help fix the questions and answers so they sound right when we read them aloud?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - Presentation My Amusement Park Minibook

details: My Amusement Park Minibook develops students’ use of past-tense key phrases and feeling adjectives to describe amusement-park experiences in a minibook.
Look for correct sticker placement, complete past-tense sentences, accurate use of feeling words, neat handwriting, and confident sharing of the minibook.
“I had so much fun that I want to make a minibook. Do you know what that is? Each page should show something exciting we did. Let’s fill it in and share it just like a real little storybook!”
